title: Screening gist + risk map — runtime candidate
content:
High-level: quick capture of impressions after loop. This is messy intentionally — working notes for follow-up and for shaping the take-home/pairing task.

Summary (1 sentence): Solid systems engineer, strong distro of debugging instincts around memory/IPC issues, uncertain on latency- sensitive kernel selection decisions and tradeoffs for quantized 4-bit models. Would be strong with a short project to exercise inference kernel/quantization reasoning.

Signals I liked:
- Walked through a non-trivial perf incident and traced root cause to cache sharding imbalance; good intuition about hardware constraints and observed tradeoffs.
- Comfortable with Linux perf/topology, NUMA, and basic CUDA observability (nvprof / nsight mention).
- Clear communicator when sketching high-level mitigation strategy (fallback routing, conservative batching) — good SRE collaboration fit.

Concerns / Risks (ranked):
1) Quantization and kernel tradeoffs (MED): Could describe tradeoffs conceptually but struggled to map them to concrete latency vs quality numbers or how to measure regression in CI. Needs a short concrete exercise.
2) Model compilation familiarity (LOW-MED): Knows concept of kernel fusion and autotuning but hasn't shipped a compilation pipeline or e2e model onboarding flow. Might need mentorship early.
3) Ownership style (SMALL): Prefers deep debugging vs productizing; check for willingness to push smaller cross-team deliverables.

Suggested next-step assessment (quick, <1 week):
- Pairing task: 90 minute session where we give a tiny Llama-like model (small weights), two compiled variants (fp16 vs int4), and a micro-benchmark harness. Ask candidate to:
  1) reproduce a surprising latency regression in the harness,
  2) propose two mitigation strategies (one config-level, one infra-level),
  3) sketch a minimal metric to detect regressions automatically.
- Follow-up deliverable: 1-page notes and a short script they modify (or pseudo-patch) to demonstrate config change.

Scoring (my gut):
- Systems debugging: 4/5
- Inference-specific engineering (compilation/quant): 3/5
- Communicates tradeoffs: 4/5
- Collaboration / cross-team: 4/5
- Overall hire recommendation: hire-with-condition (mentor first 3 months + kernel exposure project)

Concrete follow-ups I will do before final write-up:
- Share a template short task repo (ENG-4321 sandbox) and verify they can run harness locally (Asha will help with access).
- Ask Diego to prepare 2 short logs that replicate the cache-shard scenario we discussed (so candidate can point to concrete artifacts in pair session).

Notes to self for final passback (bullet prompts):
- Ask them how they'd measure "quality regression" after switching to int4 for a specific endpoint (ideas: likelihood delta vs small eval set, token-level logprob distribution shift, human eval triage). If answer uses only intuition -> flag for follow-up.
- Push for an example where they balanced throughput vs p95 tail (want real numbers and a lifting of assumptions).
- Confirm whether they have an opinionated preference for router/fallback (model variants vs region) and why.

Quick checklist for offer draft (if moving forward):
- Mentorship plan: pair with kernel team for 1:1s (6 weeks), join weekly compilation syncs.
- Early project: 3-week kernel tuning project with defined success metric (p95 reduced by X% or cost/token reduction Y).

Random contextual memory: mentioned previous employer used a homegrown autotuner that reduced latency variability by ~30% — follow up to ask for concrete numbers and if they owned parts of it.

Open questions for candidate at next touch:
- Have you shipped automated quality checks for quantized models? Where and how?
- Do you prefer infra-level solutions (routing/replicas) or model-level changes when under latency pressure?

End of notes.

Small log/links I pointed them to during screen:
- Quick-start sandbox repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-4321-sandbox
- Confluence: /display/INF/quantization-eval-guidelines (shared after pairing)
- Example small benchmark: scripts/bench_latency.py (in sandbox repo)

-- Riley
